_comment: Choicer Voicer lines. One iconic moment per entry — the thing players take
turns performing into their own microphone.
FIELDS
id          unique; shares room.usedVideoIds with every other pool, so it
must not look like a YouTube id. Prefix vo-.
quote       the line, exactly as it is said. This is PUBLIC — it goes out
on room:updated the moment the round starts, because everyone
has to know what they are performing.
source      who said it and where. Public, same reason: half the
performance is knowing the delivery.
youtube     PASTE THE URL STRAIGHT FROM THE ADDRESS BAR. Any form works —
youtu.be/ID, watch?v=ID, /shorts/ID, /embed/ID — and a ?t= on
the end is read as the start time. This is what the room hears
at the top of the round and what REPLAY plays again.
youtubeId   the bare 11-character id, if you would rather write that. Wins
over `youtube` when both are set. Anything that is not exactly
11 characters is refused and logged, because a typo here plays
somebody else's video and reports nothing.
start/end   seconds. Trim to the line and nothing else — the room is
listening to one moment, not the scene around it.
peaks       96 numbers, 0..1: the ORIGINAL waveform, precomputed. Needed
for a YouTube line, because an embed is a cross-origin iframe
and the page cannot read a single sample out of it. Written by
the fingerprint script from a local copy of the audio.
audio       optional same-origin path under public/, e.g.
/audio/voicelines/x.wav. An alternative to YouTube rather than
a companion to it: the client can decode this one, so it draws
its own waveform and needs no `peaks`. YouTube wins when both
are set.
fingerprint optional, and the important one. 384 numbers produced by
scripts/fingerprint-voiceline.ts from the original audio.
When present the round scores every take against it, which is
what the mode is actually for.
THE YOUTUBE IDS ARE BLANK ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE ONE JOB LEFT.
A YouTube id is eleven opaque characters. There is no way to derive one
from a film title, and a wrong one does not error — it plays a different
video, or a deleted one, with nothing reported anywhere. So they are left
empty rather than guessed. Find each moment, paste the watch URL into
`youtube`, and the round plays it. Until then a line runs off its quote
alone, which is still playable — the room performs from memory.
ADDING A LINE
1. Add an entry here with id + quote + source, and paste a `youtube` URL.
2. That is enough to play. For SCORING AGAINST THE ORIGINAL you also need a
local copy of the audio, because the embed cannot be measured:
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 48000 -t 4 public/audio/voicelines/<id>.wav
npm run voicer:fingerprint -- --in public/audio/voicelines/<id>.wav --id <id> --write
which fills in `fingerprint`, `peaks` and `audio` for you. Add
--no-audio when the embed is the real original and the local file is
only there to be measured.
SCORING, AND WHY fingerprint IS OPTIONAL
With a fingerprint: each take is scored against the real recording. This
is the mode as designed and the reference is the answer key, so it stays
server-side and never rides a broadcast.
Without one: the round still plays, and each take is scored against the
average of everybody else's — 'who matched what the room agreed the line
sounds like'. That is a genuine game and it is what makes this pool
playable before anybody has done the audio work, but it is NOT a
measurement against the original. The results screen says which was used.
THE WAVs ON DISK ARE MACHINE-GENERATED PLACEHOLDERS.
The local text-to-speech voice reading each line, committed so the mode is
playable and testable out of the box — the listen beat, the overlaid
waveforms, the replay control and reference scoring all work end to end
against them. They are a robot reading the words, not the iconic delivery.
Replace them with the real clips and re-run step 2, or delete them and let
the YouTube embed be the original.
AUTHORING RULES
1. The line must be short. Under about four seconds. Twenty-four time
slices spread over a long speech puts a whole sentence in one slice and
every take scores the same.
2. It must be iconic enough that the room can already hear it. If people
need the clip to know how it goes, the round is a listening exercise.
3. It wants a distinctive DELIVERY, not just distinctive words. The score
is frequency shape over time — pitch, emphasis, rhythm. A flatly
delivered famous line gives every player the same fingerprint.
4. Prefer lines with a strong contour: a rise, a break, a shout at a
particular point. Those are what a fingerprint can actually see.

lines.quote: I am the one who knocks!
My name is Maximus Decimus Meridius.
That's one small step for man.
Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn.
You're gonna need a bigger boat.
Say hello to my little friend!
I'm the king of the world!
I have a very particular set of skills.
I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse.
Nobody puts Baby in a corner.
